title: Files & I/O
hook: Your code rarely talks to the disk itself — it asks the OS, and then everyone waits.

steps.caption: The app calls read/write. That becomes a system call into the OS.

nodeCaptions.app: User code isn’t allowed to poke device registers directly (on modern OSes).
nodeCaptions.os: The kernel enforces permissions and manages the device.

steps.caption: The OS talks to the disk. This can take ages compared to RAM.

nodeCaptions.disk: Hardware delay dominates. The CPU may run something else meanwhile.

steps.caption: Data returns through the OS to the app.

nodeCaptions.app: From the app’s view it was one read() — the wait was real either way.

takeaways: File I/O is mediated by the OS for safety and abstraction.
Disk latency is why I/O-bound programs feel different from CPU-bound ones.
Async I/O and caching exist to hide some of that wait.

quiz.question: Who usually performs the actual disk operation when your app reads a file?
choices: The operating system (kernel), on the app’s behalf
quiz.explanation: System calls hand the request to the kernel, which drives the device.
